questions.stem: National Highways in India are constructed and maintained by
options: State Public Works Departments and state road boards acting independently of the Centre
District Boards (Zila Parishads) and municipal bodies of the major towns on the route
The Central Government through agencies such as the NHAI
Village panchayats and local self-help groups
questions.explanation: National Highways link distant parts of the country and are the responsibility of the Central Government, which builds and maintains them through agencies such as the National Highways Authority of India. State highways are looked after by states, district roads by districts and rural roads by local bodies.

optionRationale.1: State Public Works Departments look after state highways.
optionRationale.2: District roads are the responsibility of district bodies, not the National Highways.
optionRationale.4: Village panchayats look after rural roads.

questions.stem: The Border Roads Organisation mainly builds roads in
options: remote border and mountainous areas, important for defence and development
central business districts of metropolitan cities, where traffic is heavy and land is costly
river deltas for the movement of ships only
irrigated plains of the Punjab where roads already exist in plenty
questions.explanation: The Border Roads Organisation builds and maintains roads in remote border regions, many of them in mountains, to support defence movement and to bring development to such areas. Its work is concentrated on difficult terrain where other agencies find it hard to build.

optionRationale.2: City centres are served by municipal and state agencies.
optionRationale.3: Roads are not meant for ships, and delta roads are not its main task.
optionRationale.4: Densely networked plains are not its main concern.

questions.objective: Recall the role of the Border Roads Organisation

questions.stem: Match the mode of transport in List-I with its main strength in List-II.

right: I. Carry oil and gas continuously
II. Fastest and reach remote areas
IV. Best for bulk goods over long distances

questions.explanation: Roads give door-to-door service, railways are best for bulk goods over long distances, pipelines carry oil and gas continuously with low running cost, and airways are the fastest and can reach remote or inaccessible areas. So A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

optionRationale.1: This code gives roads the bulk-goods strength and railways the door-to-door one.
optionRationale.2: This code gives roads the pipeline strength and pipelines the door-to-door one.
optionRationale.3: This code gives railways the speed of airways and pipelines the bulk-goods strength.

questions.objective: Match transport modes with their strengths

questions.stem: A railway line in which the rails are one metre apart is called
questions.explanation: Gauge is the distance between the two rails. Metre gauge is exactly one metre, while broad gauge in India is 1.676 m. Narrow gauge is less than one metre, and standard gauge is 1.435 m, used in much of the rest of the world.

optionRationale.1: Narrow gauge is narrower than one metre.
optionRationale.3: Broad gauge in India is 1.676 m, wider than one metre.
optionRationale.4: Standard gauge is 1.435 m, not one metre.

questions.stem: The Konkan Railway, built along the western coast of India, runs
options: along the east coast between Chennai and Kolkata
along the west coast through Maharashtra, Goa and Karnataka
across the Ganga plain from Delhi to Patna
through the Thar desert from Jaisalmer to Jodhpur
questions.explanation: The Konkan Railway is a west coast line that passes through Maharashtra, Goa and Karnataka, crossing many rivers, tunnels and hills of the Western Ghats region. It shortened the rail distance along the west coast and connected coastal towns that had little rail service earlier.

optionRationale.1: The east coast has a different rail line.
optionRationale.3: The Ganga plain is served by other trunk lines.
optionRationale.4: The Konkan line lies in the coastal Western Ghats region, not the desert.

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): Railways are the most suitable mode for carrying fresh flowers over short distances in India.
Reason (R): Railways are best suited for carrying bulky goods and passengers over long distances.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Railways have an advantage in bulk and long-distance movement, so R is true. Fresh flowers are light, perishable and high in value, and over short distances roads, with door-to-door delivery, or air for long distances, are better. Hence A is false.

optionRationale.1: A is false, so R cannot explain it.
optionRationale.2: A is not true, so this option is wrong.
optionRationale.3: R is true, so the option calling it false is wrong.

questions.objective: Match goods with suitable transport modes

questions.stem:
Consider the statements.
A. The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana aims to connect villages with all-weather roads.
B. State highways link state capitals with district headquarters and important towns.
C. District roads are built and maintained by the Central Government.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana is a rural road programme for connecting villages, and state highways join state capitals with district headquarters and other towns, so A and B are correct. Statement C is wrong because district roads are looked after by district authorities, not by the Centre.

optionRationale.2: C is false, so any option with C is wrong.
optionRationale.3: C is false and the option leaves out B.
optionRationale.4: C is false, so all three cannot be correct.

questions.objective: Evaluate statements on the Indian road system

questions.stem: Marmagao port in Goa is important chiefly for the export of
questions.explanation: Marmagao in Goa is a leading port for the export of iron ore, which is mined in the hinterland of Goa and Karnataka and carried to the port for shipment, mainly to overseas steel makers. Tea, cotton goods and petroleum products move mostly through other ports.

optionRationale.1: Tea is not the main commodity of Marmagao.
optionRationale.2: Cotton textiles are not its chief export.
optionRationale.4: Petroleum products are handled mainly at other ports.

questions.stem: Satellite (relief) ports such as Haldia and Jawaharlal Nehru Port were developed mainly to
options: replace road transport with sea transport inside the cities and bring down the number of vehicles
serve only the navy and the defence forces of the country along the coast
export only fresh flowers by sea
reduce congestion at the older parent ports of Kolkata and Mumbai
questions.explanation: Haldia was developed as a subsidiary port to relieve the heavy pressure on Kolkata, and Jawaharlal Nehru Port at Nhava Sheva was developed to relieve Mumbai. Both handle part of the cargo so that the parent ports do not become congested.

optionRationale.1: They are sea ports and do not replace city road transport.
optionRationale.2: They are commercial cargo ports, not naval bases.
optionRationale.3: Flowers are not their main cargo.

questions.objective: Explain why relief ports were built

questions.stem: A consignment must travel 900 km. By road it moves at an average of 45 km per hour and by air at 450 km per hour. How many hours does the air route save?
questions.explanation: Time by road = 900 / 45 = 20 hours. Time by air = 900 / 450 = 2 hours. The saving is 20 - 2 = 18 hours. The option 20 hours is the road time alone, not the saving.

optionRationale.1: 10 hours is not the difference of the two times.
optionRationale.3: 20 hours is the road time, not the time saved.
optionRationale.4: 22 hours adds the two times instead of subtracting them.

questions.objective: Compare travel times by different modes

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): India's exports now include manufactured goods and software services, and not only agricultural goods.
Reason (R): India does not import any petroleum products.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: India's export basket has broadened from raw and agricultural goods to include manufactures, engineering goods and software services, so A is true. R is false because petroleum and crude oil are among India's major imports. Hence A is true and R is false.

optionRationale.1: R is false, so it cannot explain A.
optionRationale.2: R is false, so the option claiming both are true is wrong.
optionRationale.4: A is true, so the option calling it false is wrong.

questions.objective: Describe the changing composition of India's trade

questions.stem: A country imports goods worth 500 units every year. Its exports rise from 400 units to 460 units while imports stay the same. By what percentage does its trade deficit fall?
questions.explanation: The deficit is imports minus exports. At first it is 500 - 400 = 100 units, and afterwards it is 500 - 460 = 40 units. The fall is 60 units, and 60/100 x 100 = 60 per cent. The new deficit of 40 is only the remaining part.

optionRationale.2: 40 is the remaining deficit in units, not the percentage fall.
optionRationale.3: 15 per cent is the rise in exports (60/400), not the fall in the deficit.
optionRationale.4: 6 per cent does not follow from 60 out of 100.

questions.stem:
Consider the statements on communication.
A. INSAT is a multipurpose satellite system of India.
B. Mass communication includes radio, television and newspapers.
C. Personal communication consists only of newspapers.
D. The internet allows information to be exchanged across the world.
Which are correct?
questions.explanation: INSAT is a multipurpose satellite system, mass communication includes radio, television and newspapers, and the internet links users across the world, so A, B and D are correct. Statement C is false, because personal communication includes letters, telephone and email, not only newspapers.

optionRationale.2: C is false, and this option also omits B and D.
optionRationale.3: C is false, so this option cannot be right.
optionRationale.4: C is false, so all four cannot be correct.

questions.stem: An urgent medical sample has to be sent quickly from Delhi to Port Blair in the Andaman Islands. The most suitable mode is
questions.explanation: The Andaman Islands lie far from the mainland across the sea. Air transport is the fastest mode and can reach islands, so it is the best choice for an urgent, light and high-value consignment. Roads cannot cross the sea, waterways are slow and pipelines carry only fluids.

optionRationale.1: Roads cannot cross the sea to the islands.
optionRationale.2: Inland waterways are slow and are not meant for the sea crossing.
optionRationale.4: Pipelines carry only liquids and gases.

questions.objective: Choose a transport mode for an urgent consignment

questions.stem: Which factor best explains the high density of railways in the northern plains of India?
options: Dense forests and high mountains which make track building easy
Level land, dense population and active farming and industry
The absence of rivers, so no bridges are required
Very low population, so little connectivity is needed
questions.explanation: Railways are cheapest to build on flat land. The northern plains are level, densely populated and productive in farming and industry, so they generate heavy traffic and justify a dense network. Forests, mountains and low population make building costly or traffic poor.

optionRationale.1: Forests and mountains make building difficult and costly.
optionRationale.3: The plains have many large rivers, which need bridges.
optionRationale.4: The northern plains are among the most densely populated regions.

questions.objective: Relate railway density to physical and economic factors

questions.stem: Pipelines have a high initial cost but a low running cost, so they are most economical when
options: small irregular loads must go to many scattered destinations in different directions
perishable goods need door-to-door delivery to many different customers
the route has to be changed every season
a large volume of oil or gas flows steadily along a fixed route for years
questions.explanation: A large part of the cost of a pipeline is spent at the start, so it is worthwhile only when a large and steady flow of liquid or gas will use the same route for many years. Then the cost per unit carried becomes low. Variable or scattered loads suit roads better.

optionRationale.1: Small irregular loads to many places suit road transport.
optionRationale.2: Door-to-door delivery is a feature of road transport.
optionRationale.3: A pipeline is fixed and cannot be moved seasonally.

questions.stem: The hinterland of a port is most likely to expand when
options: it is cut off from railways and highways
its harbour becomes shallow due to silting
the port stops handling any cargo
efficient road, rail and inland-waterway links to the interior are built
questions.explanation: A hinterland is the area that supplies exports and receives imports through a port. Good road, rail and waterway links make it easy and cheap to bring goods from farther inland, so the area served grows. Isolation, silting or the stoppage of cargo shrinks it.

optionRationale.1: Loss of road and rail links shrinks the hinterland.
optionRationale.2: A silted harbour handles fewer ships and loses traffic.
optionRationale.3: A port with no cargo has no functioning hinterland.

questions.objective: Relate hinterland size to transport links

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): India's foreign trade has shifted over time towards manufactured goods and services.
Reason (R): Most of India's foreign trade by volume is carried through seaports.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Industrial growth and the rise of software and other services have changed the composition of India's trade, so A is true. It is also true that most trade by volume goes by sea. But the use of seaports tells us how goods move and not why the composition changed.

optionRationale.1: The mode of carriage does not explain the change in the kind of goods traded.
optionRationale.3: R is true, so the option calling it false is wrong.
optionRationale.4: A is true, so the option calling it false is wrong.

questions.objective: Distinguish composition of trade from mode of carriage
